title: Mixed-parity cubic audit: graph obstruction and physical scaling
analyticClaims: For a finite carrier set S in gZ, the carrier Cayley graph is bipartite exactly when every reduced carrier r/g is odd.
The set {1,4} is non-bipartite although it has no signed triangle; the two-color obstruction is therefore broader than the triangle count.
For S_R={R,...,3R-1}, the positive ordered relations a+b=c number R(R+1)/2, the signed ordered triangles number 3R(R+1), and the uncorrected aligned coefficient has magnitude 3R(R+1)/sqrt(2).
finiteDiagnostics: The producer and independent routes use R=4,8,16,32,64 and construct one exact complex root at tau=R^-3.
The measured raw cubic delta integral |h P0 V^2 F| has a last-three-point log slope near 1.950.
After the declared physical lift, the normalized true cubic has a last-three-point log slope near -0.737; the R^-2/3 line is a scaling guide.
The universal R^-4/9(1+log R)^-2/3 envelope is stated as an analytic theorem-rate reference and is not fitted to this finite family.
claimBoundary: The figure combines an exact carrier-graph classification with binary64 finite corroboration for one triangle-rich mixed-parity block. The numerical launch constructs one complex root only, does not enumerate complete roots, and does not invoke the real Rolle complete-root corollary. It does not prove an asymptotic estimate, a general physical trace theorem, blow-up, continuation, or three-dimensional Navier-Stokes regularity.
